Director’s Note

The Wizard of Oz is a show that everyone knows, or has decided ideas about. It can be daunting to do any kind of re-imagining of something so iconic. However, one of the things that is special about live theater is that every production allows the artistic team to put their own spin on the story.

In the film, Dorothy’s life in Kansas is gray. We often think this is to reflect how staid her life is in Kansas compared to the vibrancy of Oz. In reality, it was a way to show off the new technicolor process as films were being shot for the first time. To my mind, Dorothy spends the entire show trying to get home to Kansas, so we chose not to avoid color.

We also had to decide on an approach to Dorothy’s visit to Oz. Does Dorothy literally travel to Oz in person, as is what clearly happens in the book? Or does she take a knock on the head and imagine it all, as is strongly implied in the film?

Traditionally, the friends Dorothy meets in Oz are played by the same actors that play the people she knows from Kansas. Since we try to give as many actors opportunities to perform as possible, we’ve taken a different approach. After all, if Dorothy has a concussion and goes to an imaginary land anything can happen. Look for “easter eggs” in Kansas that appear again in Oz!

The Wizard of Oz was my first show. I was a munchkin in the 4th grade, and wore roller skates. It was fun then, and it’s still fun working with the wonderful team of artists that put it together. We hope you enjoy it!

Awards

Judy Robe Award

It has long been a tradition on Broadway to pass along a robe from show to show to honor the member of the ensemble who has been in the most productions. PYT’s tradition has been to pass a robe to a member of the ensemble who best embodies PYT’s values of teamwork, responsibility and positivity. PYT has named this award in honor of long-term board member and volunteer Judy Meyer. Over the hundreds of productions where Judy volunteered, she personified these values, and served as an excellent role model for thousands of PYT performers.

The production staff considers attitude, improvement and dedication in selecting the recipient, who dons the robe and circles around the cast for good luck before curtain. Later, the recipient attaches a memento, and presents the robe to their successor.

PYT is pleased to present this production’s Judy Robe to:

Sophia Ardelean

See all past recipients at pytnet.org/about/judy-robe

Staff & Creative Team Biographies

KAREN SIMPSON (Director/Set Designer) Karen is PYT’s Executive Artistic Director and resident playwright. In her more than twenty-five years with PYT she’s written over 25 plays, designed sets and directed numerous productions, most recently A Year With Frog and Toad and Six Teen Edition.

JENNIFER TIPTON (Choreographer) Jen is PYT’s resident choreographer, and directed and choreographed Seussical the Musical. She is also a regular director in PYT’s Stories on Stage program, where she most recently directed Dragons Love Tacos. Jen is looking forward to tackling the amazingly challenging choreo for Singin’ in the Rain next!

ROMA OLVERA (Vocal Director) Roma is the Music Director at Woodland School in Portola Valley. She is a lyric soprano and an opera librettist. Her libretto works include Xochitl and the Flowers and Harriet’s Spirit. Roma is thrilled to be vocal directing for PYT for the first time.

ANDREW CUSTER (Lighting Designer) Andrew is thrilled to return to PYT, where his passion for theater began. With over 20 years of experience, he has worked with the Bay Area Playwrights Festival, TheatreWorks, Foothill Music Theatre, and IATSE Local 16. He is excited to bring his expertise back to the community that inspired him.

RICK VAN MELL (Technical Director) Rick has been transforming the creative Director’s and Set Designer’s drawings into physical sets since 2016. The Set Build/Load-in team builds, transports and strikes the set at MVCPA. Then salvages parts for future shows, like 84 casters & 336 bolts. Enjoy the Wizard!

ALETTE MAHLER (Costume Designer) Alette has been enjoying costuming for PYT productions for many years. Miracle on 34th Street was one of her early shows. Favorites include Cats, Les Mis, Finding Nemo, and Newsies. The kiddos, the families, and her teams keep her interested in PYT.

SHIBOUNE THILL (Stage Manager/Hair and Makeup Design/Fight Choreographer) has spent over two decades contributing to 60+ productions at PYT. Starting as a performer, she expanded her talents into stage management, design, photography, sound, and electrics. Recent credits include Six and Frog and Toad. This marks her fourth journey down PYT’s yellow brick road!

MIKE ‘SHARKBAIT’ COBB (Sound Design/Producer) Mike has produced over 25 Mainstage productions for PYT and has been their in-house Sound Designer for several years. He would like to thank all the dedicated parent volunteers (especially his co-producers!) for their support of The Wizard of Oz!

DEANNE BLIGH (Producer) Deanne is thrilled to be a part of this production of The Wizard of Oz. Most recently serving as a volunteer producer for Newsies, she is passionate about being a part of musical theater. She can’t wait to watch her two boys and this incredible cast shine on stage!

ANN & BRYAN HYNECEK (Producer) Ann and Bryan Hynecek love supporting their daughter’s passion for performing. This year, they are thrilled to support behind the scenes, as volunteer producers. They are proud to travel down the yellow brick road with such a wonderful community that encourages young talent, creativity, and a love of the arts.

About Peninsula Youth Theatre

A resident company of the Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts.

Our mission: To provide outstanding theatrical learning experiences that develop leadership, emphasize responsibility and foster teamwork in a supportive, respectful and fun environment.
